q: What is a normal energy use per tonne for an MSME chemical unit?
title: MSME chemical units: energy per tonne
short: Overall 4.98 GJ, or 119 kgoe, per tonne, in BEE's energy mapping of five chemical MSME clusters, ranging from 0.44 GJ in Jamshedpur to 6.33 GJ in Ahmedabad. Product type matters more than place: averages were 9.8 GJ for API and pharma, 6.0 for dyes and pigments and 3.3 for pesticides.
audience: Owners of small chemical, dye, pesticide and bulk drug units comparing their energy use with peers

ul: Jamshedpur: 99,950 t a year, 11 kgoe (0.44 GJ) per tonne.

sections.h: By product, which is the fairer comparison
ul: API and pharma: 9.8 GJ per tonne on average.
The spread inside each group is wide, so a batch drug unit at twice the average is not unusual.

ol: Add a year of fuel in GJ: gas scm x the heat value on your bill, coal tonnes x its calorific value, and so on.
Add electricity at 3.6 MJ per kWh, its heat value. Ask any auditor which convention they use, since some count power at the fuel burned to make it.
Divide by tonnes produced in the same year and compare with your product group, not just your cluster.

p: Audits in 50 units found efficient boilers, thermic fluid heaters, air compressors and motors as the near-term fixes, and electric boilers, electric thermic fluid heaters, fluidised bed dryers in place of tray dryers and rooftop solar as the next step. It puts the sector's potential at 70,000 toe of energy and 270,000 t of CO2.

example.title: A dyes and pigments unit making 3,000 t a year
lines: Gas: 400,000 scm x 0.0398 GJ (9,500 kcal per scm on the bill) = 15,920 GJ
Energy per tonne: 19,160 / 3,000 = 6.4 GJ, close to the 6.0 average for dyes and pigments
example.note: An example unit, not a measured one: use your own bills. Gas and grid factors are our estimates, the grid at CEA's FY 2025-26 figure.

senseible: Senseible reads your gas, coal and electricity bills into yearly quantities and CO2, each linked to its bill; divide by your production and you have energy and carbon per tonne to put next to these figures.
